ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Compressed Visual Thought Tokens for Interleaved Jigsaw Reasoning
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a unified understanding-and-generation model of 7B parameters, initialised from Janus-Pro, to solve 3x3 jigsaw puzzles by alternating a short text step with a generated intermediate image of the partially assembled puzzle. Each intermediate image is encoded back as only 64 compressed tokens through a learned pooling module, instead of the full grid of visual tokens, so the sequence stays short. Train on synthetic puzzles built from COCO images and evaluate exact-match accuracy on held-out puzzles, with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare with text-only chain-of-thought, an interleaved baseline that keeps the full visual tokens, a variant that drops intermediate images, and compression to 16 and 256 tokens.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Compressed thoughts should match the full-token baseline within a few points of accuracy while cutting sequence length sharply. Accuracy could collapse once the compression is too tight to keep piece boundaries.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Interleaved Jigsaw Reasoning with Full-Resolution Visual Steps and Dense Checkpointing
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a unified understanding-and-generation model of 7B parameters, initialised from Janus-Pro, on 3x3, 4x4 and 5x5 jigsaw puzzles, alternating a text step with a generated image of the assembled puzzle at full token resolution. Train on synthetic puzzles built from COCO, ImageNet and Open Images pictures with the puzzle sizes mixed into one curriculum, and evaluate exact-match accuracy at saved checkpoints on held-out puzzles, with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare with text-only chain-of-thought, a pure image-generation baseline, a variant that drops intermediate images, and learning-rate schedules at 3 peak values over the same checkpoints.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Accuracy should rise steadily with puzzle-size mixing and plateau after most checkpoints, with gains concentrated on the smallest size. Training could become unstable at the biggest puzzle size, where sequences grow very long.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Chunked Attention over Visual States for Long Multi-Modal Reasoning Chains
PROPOSAL: Modify a unified autoregressive model so that each reasoning step attends fully to its own text and image tokens but only to a pooled summary of 32 tokens for earlier steps, turning quadratic growth in chain length into near-linear growth. Fine-tune from BAGEL on interleaved chains covering map navigation and geometry, and measure accuracy on MathVista geometry items and a navigation set of mazes, with chains of 4 to 12 steps, over 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare against full attention, a sliding window over the last 2 steps, text-only reasoning, and a variant that summarises earlier steps with the text alone.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: Chunked attention should retain accuracy on chains up to 12 steps while using far less memory than full attention. It may degrade on tasks where a late step needs fine detail from an early image.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Memory-Matched Attention Variants for Long Interleaved Chains on Reasoning Suites
PROPOSAL: Modify a unified autoregressive model so each reasoning step attends fully to its own tokens but only to a pooled summary of earlier steps, and fine-tune from BAGEL under variants of summary size and pooling rule. Train on interleaved chains covering map navigation, geometry, jigsaw and chart tasks, and measure accuracy on MathVista, MathVerse, a navigation set of mazes and a jigsaw set, with chains of 4 to 24 steps, over 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare against full attention, sliding windows of assorted lengths, text-only reasoning, and a text-only summary variant, trained to a matched token count.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: Variants should cluster within a point or two of full attention on shorter chains and separate only past 16 steps. Gains may vanish if the pooled summaries discard the geometry that later steps need.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Discarding Stale Image Tokens in the Cache During Interleaved Inference
PROPOSAL: At inference time only, evict the cached visual tokens of reasoning steps older than the previous one while keeping their text tokens, using a pretrained unified model such as Janus-Pro without retraining. Run jigsaw and map-navigation problems with chains of up to 8 steps and compare accuracy, peak memory and generation speed. Test a learned retention score, based on attention mass, that decides which image tokens to keep within a fixed budget of 30 percent, using 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare with no eviction, random eviction at the same ratio, always keeping the first image, and text-only reasoning. Include the retention score alone with no learned scorer.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Eviction should save a large part of the memory with small accuracy loss, and the attention-based score should beat random removal. It may fail if chains revisit early images, because evicted tokens cannot be recovered.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cache Pruning Policies for Interleaved Inference Evaluated on Benchmark Collections
PROPOSAL: At inference time only, evict the cached visual tokens of older reasoning steps while keeping their text tokens, comparing pruning agents on pretrained unified models such as Janus-Pro, BAGEL and Show-o without retraining. Run jigsaw, navigation, geometry and editing problems with chains of up to 16 steps and compare accuracy, peak memory and generation speed. Test learned retention scores at budgets of 10 and 60 percent, using 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare with no eviction, random eviction at matched ratios, always keeping the first image, text-only reasoning, and the retention score alone with no learned scorer, in each model, with latency measured on one fixed accelerator type.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Pruning should save most of the memory with small accuracy loss on the models, and the learned score should beat random removal. Differences between the controllers may be too small to resolve on most benchmarks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latent Visual State Vectors Instead of Rendered Images in Reasoning Chains
PROPOSAL: Replace the rendered image at each reasoning step with a short sequence of 16 continuous latent vectors that the model predicts and re-reads, and decode an image only for the final answer. Build the model on a Qwen2.5-VL backbone with a lightweight diffusion head, and train on topographic contour maps paired with landscape images for the generation task and on jigsaw puzzles for the understanding task, with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare against rendered intermediate images, text-only reasoning, and latent vectors without a reconstruction loss. Ablate latent lengths of 4, 16 and 64 vectors.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Latent states should reach most of the accuracy of rendered images at a small fraction of the tokens. They may lose precision on fine spatial detail such as contour spacing, where an explicit image helps.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Continuous Latent Visual Steps Versus Rendered Images over Mixed Training Data
PROPOSAL: Replace the rendered image at each reasoning step with a sequence of 32 continuous latent vectors that the model predicts and re-reads, and decode an image only in the final answer. Build models on Qwen2.5-VL backbones of 3 sizes with a diffusion head, and train on topographic contour maps, jigsaw puzzles, edited photographs and geometry figures, with a separate model per mixture, with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare against rendered intermediate images, text-only reasoning, latent vectors without a reconstruction loss, and other latent lengths, retrained at each backbone size and compared at matched decoding settings.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Latent states should keep most of the rendered-image accuracy at a small fraction of the tokens at all sizes. Gains offered by bigger backbones may be minor if the diffusion head is the limiting part.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-Modality Loss Weighting to Stabilise Interleaved Image-Text Training
PROPOSAL: Diagnose instability in a unified model trained on interleaved chains by logging gradient norms separately for text tokens and image tokens, which differ in scale and speed of convergence. Train a 7B model from BAGEL with a per-modality loss weight that is updated using the ratio of recent gradient norms, plus gradient clipping at the modality level, on interleaved chains for navigation and geometry, over 3 seeds. Report loss spikes and final accuracy on held-out chains.
CONTROLS: Compare with a fixed equal weighting, fixed weights tuned by hand, global gradient clipping only at norm 1.0, and training on text alone followed by image tokens.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: Adaptive weighting should cut loss spikes and improve accuracy on long chains. It could fail if instability comes from the long context itself, which weighting cannot repair.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training Stability Study of Interleaved Chains with Optimiser and Schedule Settings
PROPOSAL: Diagnose instability in unified models trained on interleaved chains by logging gradient norms separately for text and image tokens at frequent points in training. Train 7B models from BAGEL and Janus-Pro under loss-weighting rules and 3 optimiser settings with modality-level gradient clipping, on interleaved chains for navigation, geometry, jigsaw and editing, over 3 seeds. Report loss spikes and final accuracy on held-out chains of each task.
CONTROLS: Compare with fixed equal weighting, hand-tuned fixed weights, global gradient clipping only, text-first then image training, and two warmup lengths in each setting.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: Adaptive weighting should cut loss spikes in most settings, with warmup length changing little once clipping is in place. The grid may reveal that instability stems from context length that none of the settings repairs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Staged Curriculum from Short to Long Chains for Reasoning-Driven Image Generation
PROPOSAL: Train a unified model for reasoning-driven text-to-image generation in stages, starting from prompts that need one reasoning step and moving to prompts that need up to 5 interleaved steps, such as placing objects by a stated spatial rule or counting items under a stated constraint. Fine-tune from Janus-Pro on a prompt set and evaluate on WISE and T2I-ReasonBench, using 3 seeds, scoring consistency with the prompt and with the intermediate sketches.
CONTROLS: Compare with training on the mixed-length data from the start, training on long chains only, and a text-only reasoning variant that skips sketches. Ablate the stage lengths.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: The curriculum should help most on prompts that need many steps and cost little on short ones. It might give no gain if the model already learns long chains from the mixed data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Stage Curricula over Prompt Families for Reasoning-Driven Image Generation
PROPOSAL: Train unified models for reasoning-driven text-to-image generation in stages, starting from prompts that need one reasoning step and moving to prompts that need up to 12 interleaved steps, grouped into families such as spatial rules, counting, physics and culture. Fine-tune from Janus-Pro and BAGEL on a prompt set and evaluate on WISE, T2I-ReasonBench and GenEval, using 3 seeds, scoring consistency with the prompt and with the intermediate sketches.
CONTROLS: Compare with mixed-length training from the start, long chains only, a text-only variant that skips sketches, and other stage lengths, rerun on the families with matched decoding settings.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: The curriculum should help on prompts that need many steps and cost little on short ones, though per-family differences may be small. It might give no gain if the model learns long chains from the mixed data alone.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Stepwise Instruction-Based Image Editing with a Single Unified Model
PROPOSAL: Break a complex editing instruction into a chain of short edits, generated and verified inside one unified model so that each edited image becomes the visual state for the next reasoning step. Fine-tune from BAGEL on editing instructions with multi-part requests, and evaluate on GEdit-Bench and ImgEdit with 3 seeds, scoring instruction adherence and preservation of unedited content in the source photographs.
CONTROLS: Compare with one-shot editing driven by the original instruction, an external editing model driven by a separate planner, and a chain with no verification step. Ablate the maximum chain length of 2, 4 and 6.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Stepwise editing should help on multi-part instructions and match one-shot editing on simple ones. Errors may compound along the chain, hurting preservation of unedited content.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Stepwise Editing Chains Evaluated on Editing Suites with Planners and Verifiers
PROPOSAL: Break a complex editing instruction into a chain of short edits, generated and verified inside one unified model so that each edited image becomes the visual state over the next reasoning step. Fine-tune from BAGEL, Janus-Pro and Show-o on editing instructions with multi-part requests, and evaluate on GEdit-Bench, ImgEdit, EmuEdit and MagicBrush with 3 seeds, scoring instruction adherence and preservation with automatic metrics and a rater panel.
CONTROLS: Compare with one-shot editing, external editing models driven by separate planners, a chain with no verification, and chain lengths of 2, 4, 6 and 8 on the models and suites.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Stepwise editing should help on multi-part instructions and match one-shot editing on simple ones. Results may be hard to separate across the suites if most instructions are single-part.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Geometry Reasoning with Generated Auxiliary Diagrams in a Unified Model
PROPOSAL: Train a unified model to draw auxiliary construction lines or marks on a geometry figure as an intermediate image, then continue reasoning from the redrawn figure. Fine-tune from a 7B unified model on geometry problems with synthesised diagram edits that add auxiliary segments and angle marks, and evaluate on MathVista geometry items and a held-out problem set, over 3 seeds, scoring final answer accuracy and the correctness of the drawn construction.
CONTROLS: Compare with text-only reasoning, programmatic drawing with a plotting library, a separate image generator coupled to the reasoning model, and a variant trained on final answers alone.
COST: 2800
PREDICTION: Generated diagrams should lift accuracy on problems that need a construction and leave others unchanged. Drawn constructions may be wrong in position, so correct reasoning could still end in the wrong answer.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Auxiliary Diagram Generation for Geometry Evaluated on Mathematics Collections
PROPOSAL: Train unified models to propose candidate auxiliary-line overlays on a geometry figure, render each candidate as an intermediate image, and let a learned verifier choose which redrawn figure to reason from. Fine-tune from unified models of 7B and 14B parameters on geometry and chart problems with synthesised diagram edits, and evaluate on MathVista, MathVerse, GeoQA and a held-out problem set, over 3 seeds, scoring final answer accuracy and the correctness of the drawn construction.
CONTROLS: Compare with text-only reasoning, programmatic drawing with a plotting library, a separate image generator coupled to the reasoning model, and variants trained on final answers alone at both model sizes.
COST: 2800
PREDICTION: Generated diagrams should lift accuracy on problems that need a construction and leave others unchanged. The gain may shrink at the bigger model size, where text reasoning already solves most items.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint Training of Reasoning-Driven Generation and Visual Understanding in One Model
PROPOSAL: Train a single 14B unified model on a mixture of reasoning-driven text-to-image data, editing data, jigsaw puzzles and topographic-map landscape generation, with interleaved image-text chains and compressed visual states of 64 tokens per step. Start from BAGEL and run 200000 optimisation steps, then evaluate on WISE, GEdit-Bench, a jigsaw set and a contour-map landscape set, using 3 seeds, to test whether understanding and generation improve each other.
CONTROLS: Compare with separate models trained on each task, a model trained on the understanding tasks only, a model trained on the generation tasks only, and a mixture with text-only reasoning.
COST: 5000
PREDICTION: Joint training should beat separate models on tasks that share visual state transitions, with the largest gain on jigsaw. Tasks may interfere with each other if the mixture ratios are poorly chosen.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mixture Ratio Search for Joint Reasoning, Generation and Understanding Training
PROPOSAL: Train unified models of 7B and 14B parameters on mixtures of reasoning-driven text-to-image data, editing data, jigsaw puzzles, geometry and topographic-map landscape generation, with interleaved image-text chains and compressed visual states at 64 tokens per step. Start from BAGEL and run mixture ratios for 200000 optimisation steps, then evaluate on WISE, GEdit-Bench, MathVista, a jigsaw set and a contour-map landscape set, using 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare with separate models trained per task, models trained on understanding only or generation only, text-only mixtures, and a uniform mixture rerun at alternative learning rates.
COST: 5000
PREDICTION: Joint training should beat separate models on tasks that share visual state transitions, with the largest gain on jigsaw. Mixture ratios may matter little once data volume is high, leaving the search uninformative.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distilling Long Interleaved Chains into Adaptive-Length Reasoning
PROPOSAL: Distil a teacher that always runs a long interleaved chain into a student that learns the moment to stop, using a halting head trained on whether the answer would change if the chain continued. Use BAGEL as the base and teacher chains of up to 10 steps for jigsaw, navigation and landscape tasks of varied difficulty, and evaluate accuracy and average chain length on held-out problems, with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare with the fixed-length teacher, a student with fixed length 3, a student that halts at a confidence threshold with no learned head, and a text-only adaptive-length model.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The student should keep teacher accuracy with a much shorter average chain, using short chains on easy problems. It may halt too early on hard jigsaw puzzles, where the answer changes late.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive-Length Distillation with Teachers of Different Sizes and Difficulty Tiers
PROPOSAL: Distil teachers that always run a long interleaved chain into students that learn the moment to stop, using a halting head trained on whether the answer would change if the chain continued. Use BAGEL and Janus-Pro as bases and teacher chains for jigsaw, navigation, geometry and landscape tasks across difficulty tiers, and evaluate accuracy and average chain length on held-out problems, with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare with fixed-length teachers, students with fixed lengths, students that halt at a confidence threshold with no learned head, and text-only adaptive models, by tier.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Students should keep teacher accuracy with a much shorter average chain, using short chains on easy tiers. They may halt too early on the hardest tier, where the answer changes late.
